summary: Covered by the dedicated country dossier, which located no North-Rhine-Westphalian trans statute, ordinance, enforcement series or event-security finding; the largest Land by population operates on the national federal framework (federal criminal law, the general equality act, the 2024 self-determination law administered through its registry offices).

sources.summary: NOTE: page not retrievable at fetch time (anti-bot 'Access denied' interstitial); per the country dossier this 16 July 2026 France24/wire report covers the neo-Nazi prisoner (the 'Liebich' case) placed in a men's prison despite a legal gender change - the event that drove Saxony, Saxony-Anhalt and Thuringia to launch a Bundesrat initiative to tighten the federal Self-Determination Act. Framework-level for all Länder.

Verfassungsblog constitutional-law essay (Clara Wellhäußer, 18 March 2026) on Länder prison-execution reforms for trans inmates: a majority of the 16 states have replaced placement rules unchanged since the 1970s (naming Rhineland-Palatinate's § 17 in force 1 March 2026, plus Bavaria, Saxony, Hamburg), all anchoring placement to the registry sex entry; the author deems the approach constitutionally avoidable and some versions doubtful. National framework analysis; this Land is not among the named reformers.

DW report (23 August 2023) on trans inmates in German prisons (the Penelope Frank case): the prison-staff union reports men's prisons inadequately prepared and understaffed (~2,000 officer shortage; ~60,000 inmates in nearly 200 facilities); prisons are Länder jurisdiction, some states with special facilities or guidelines. National framework context.
